data.title: Fed Eyes Hedge Fund Leverage and AI Valuations as Risks — WSJ
data.description:
By Dylan Tokar

Highly leveraged hedge funds and pressures from elevated valuations of artificial intelligence companies are at the top of the Federal Reserve Board's list of potential risks to the financial sector.

The Fed identifies broad categories of risks in an annual financial stability report. Here are a few takeaways from the latest report, released Friday:

  • Hedge-fund leverage: Leverage of hedge funds reached the highest level since data became available in 2013, the Fed said. In contrast, the banking system is in a much better place than it was before the 2008 financial crisis, as banks have continued to modestly reduce their interest-rate risk.
  • Asset valuations: Asset valuations, in particular in equities, continued to be elevated, in large part due to market enthusiasm around AI. The central bank noted that some of the enthusiasm was moderated by concerns over capital expenditures and debt issuance plans. Along with equities, the Fed also noted climbing Treasury yields and increased volatility in the bond markets.
  • Private-credit redemptions: Funding risks remained moderate, the Fed said, noting that while redemption requests at some private-credit firms are elevated, they have been recently trending downward.

The Fed outlined several scenarios where one of the risks it had identified causes instability, including one where an unexpected downturn in corporate earnings sparks declines in corporate asset valuations-for example in the AI sector.

Another involved disruptive cyberattacks, including the potential for LLMs and agentic systems to exploit vulnerabilities in the financial system.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Trinity Place Holdings Inc. Reports Third Quarter Financial Results
data.description:
Trinity Place Holdings Inc. (OTC PINK: TPHS) (the "Company," "we," "our," or "us") today announced operating results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

The Company is an intellectual property holding, investment, and commercialization company. We own and control a portfolio of intellectual property assets focused on the consumer sector, a legacy of our predecessor, Syms Corp. (“Syms”), including FilenesBasement.com, as well as the intellectual property associated with the Running of the Brides® event and the An Educated Consumer is Our Best Customer® slogan. Our strategy today centers on monetizing these assets through brand licensing, e-commerce initiatives, strategic partnerships, and protection and enforcement of our intellectual property rights.

Net Operating Losses

At September 30, 2026, the Company had carryforwards of federal net operating losses (“NOLs”) of approximately $352.8 million available to reduce future federal taxes. Of the Company’s federal NOLs, $224.5 million were generated prior to 2018 and may expire if unused by 2037, and $128.2 million were generated in 2018 and later years and can be carried forward indefinitely subject to an 80 percent taxable income annual limitation.

Based on management’s assessment, it is more likely than not that the deferred tax assets associated with the federal NOLs will not be realized by future taxable income or tax planning strategies. Accordingly, the Company has a valuation allowance of $74.1 million as of September 30, 2026. If our assumptions change and we determine that we will be able to realize these federal NOLs, the tax benefits relating to any reversal of the valuation allowance on deferred tax assets would be recognized as a reduction of income tax expense and an increase in the deferred tax asset.

Note that our certificate of incorporation includes a provision intended to help preserve certain tax benefits primarily associated with our NOLs. This provision generally prohibits, subject to certain exceptions, transfers of stock that would result in a person or group of persons becoming a 4.75 percent stockholder, or that would result in an increase or decrease in stock ownership by a person or group of persons that is an existing 4.75 percent stockholder.

Forward-Looking Statements

Such forward-looking statements do not guaranty future performance and are subject to various factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Undue reliance should not be placed on such forward-looking statements. The Company undertakes no obligation to publicly update or revise any forward-looking statements, or any facts, events, or circumstances after the date hereof that may bear upon forward-looking statements. Additionally, the Company does not undertake any responsibility to provide updates on the occurrence of unanticipated events which may cause actual results to differ from those expressed or implied by these forward-looking statements.

data.title: Perpetua Resources Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Project Update
data.description:
BOISE, Idaho, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Perpetua Resources Corp. (Nasdaq: PPTA) () ("Perpetua Resources" or "Perpetua" or the "Company") announced the filing of its unaudited condensed consolidated financial results for the period ended September 30, 2026. For details, please see the Company's related filing available on EDGAR and SEDAR+.

"Perpetua made significant progress in Q3 2026," said Jon Cherry, President and CEO of Perpetua Resources. "From advancing temporary and permanent worker housing to pioneering new access into the site, our Stibnite Gold Project is well positioned to move forward with disciplined execution. Our exploration drill program delivered compelling new mineralization, including multiple high-grade gold intervals and a new gold-tungsten discovery."

Webinar Update on Tuesday, November 17, 2026

Perpetua is pleased to announce that it will host a webinar on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, at 9:00 AM Mountain Time (11:00 AM Eastern Time). The webinar will feature members of the executive team and provide an update on project construction and a summary of recent exploration results. The presentation will be followed by a question & answer session. During the webinar, members of the executive team may discuss or disclose material business, financial or operational information that has not been previously publicly disclosed. The webinar may be accessed via telephone using the dial-in information provided below.

Webinar Details:

  • Title: "Perpetua Resources Advancing the Stibnite Gold Project"
  • Date: Tuesday, November 17, 2026
  • Time: 9:00 AM MT / 11:00 AM ET
  • Registration Link:https://us02web.zoom.us/j/81404359572?pwd=rLXP8kzBMsbap4hH6ZTr9Z5pCax5iJ.1 
  • Dial-in Number: +1 (301) 715-8592
  • Meeting ID: 814 0435 9572
  • Passcode: 065330

In addition to the live webinar, the webinar presentation will be posted on Perpetua's website at https://perpetuaresources.com/investors shortly before the webinar begins, and the webinar presentation will be available on Perpetua's website for at least 90 days following the event.

Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Highlights

  • Construction: Worker housing facility civil works were completed in late August 2026, and foundation installation commenced during the quarter. Work on the Burntlog Route ramped up through the summer field season, and long-lead powerline items have been ordered.
  • Exploration: The 2026 Exploration Drilling Program is complete, with more than 16,000 meters of core drilled. In August and then in November 2026, the Company reported new high-grade gold and antimony discoveries and identified a new gold-tungsten zone.
  • Financing update: Perpetua continued diligence and documentation on the $2.9 billion senior secured long-term loan from the Export-Import Bank of the United States ("U.S. EXIM") under the Make More in America Initiative, approved by the U.S. EXIM board on May 21, 2026. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027. The Company continues to advance detailed engineering, long-lead procurement, early works, critical path construction, and execution planning ahead of a final investment and construction decision. Unrestricted cash was $443.4 million as of September 30, 2026.
  • Antimony pilot plant: In July 2026, the Company commissioned a mobile modular processing plant, in partnership with Idaho National Laboratory, for pilot-scale testing to advance a secure domestic supply chain for antimony trisulfide.
  • Community: In July 2026, the Company opened a community resource and visitor information center in Yellow Pine, Idaho.

Construction Update

Perpetua completed 494,480 work hours during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, with no reportable spills and no serious injuries. Other highlights include:

  • Burntlog Route: Crews advanced construction along the alignment, removed dead timber left by past wildfires, and moved to pioneer roadwork. The year-round access road will give the Project an expanded and upgraded route capable of handling larger loads and equipment.
  • Worker Housing Facility: Treated wood foundations were installed for the kitchen, dining, and recreation modules, and a metal foundation was installed to support the dormitory buildings and the arctic corridor.
  • Powerline: Perpetua is well advanced in procuring key equipment. Substations and transformers are on order, while deliveries of power poles and ancillary equipment continue to the Company's laydown areas in Donnelly and Cascade, Idaho. Power pole installation commenced in October.

Looking ahead, Perpetua will continue to advance critical path work including bridge deliveries for Burntlog Route, installation of the worker housing facility, ongoing powerline procurement and construction, and placing orders for long-lead-time equipment.

New Exploration Results Announced

The 2026 drilling program sought to upgrade in-pit and near-pit inferred resources, extend mineralization along strike, test key underground targets, and follow up on discoveries from the 2025-2026 program. Recent highlights included:

  • Fiddle Discovery: The new Fiddle prospect, located approximately 750 meters south of the permitted Yellow Pine Pit, includes some of the most significant mineralized material encountered at the Stibnite Gold Project to date. Discovery hole SB633 returned 109.7 meters of 3.2 g/t gold and 1.1% antimony. Fiddle adds a new target area with potential to expand the Project's in-pit and near-pit resource base. The Company has since completed significant additional drilling at Fiddle, with assay results expected in the coming months.
  • Clark Tunnel Fault Zone (CTFZ): First announced in August, the CTFZ is located within or adjacent to the southeastern limits of the permitted Yellow Pine Pit. New results announced earlier this month returned near-surface, high-grade gold intercepts from recent drilling, including 25.4 meters of 4.5 g/t gold from 13 meters downhole and 25.0 meters of 2.3 g/t gold from 18 meters downhole. These results follow the drilling announced in August, which included a tungsten discovery in Hole SB597 that returned 21.3 meters of 3.2 g/t gold and 0.9% tungsten from 24 meters downhole.

Near-Term Outlook

Through the remainder of 2026 and early 2027, Perpetua is advancing early works, critical path construction, and detailed engineering for the process plant. Other initiatives include finalizing key construction and equipment contracts. With the 2026 exploration program recently completed, Perpetua expects to announce ongoing exploration results into 2027.

Website: www.perpetuaresources.com

About Perpetua Resources and the Stibnite Gold ProjectPerpetua Resources Corp., through its wholly owned subsidiaries, is focused on the exploration, site restoration and redevelopment of gold-antimony-silver deposits in the Stibnite-Yellow Pine district of central Idaho. The Stibnite Gold Project is one of the highest-grade, open-pit gold deposits in the United States and holds the only identified domestic reserve of the critical mineral antimony, which is essential to the defense, energy and manufacturing sectors. The Project is designed to apply a modern, responsible mining approach to restore a historic mine site and provide uplift to water quality, improve fish habitat access, and invest in river restoration while supporting local economic development in rural Idaho.

Quality Assurance

The exploration activities at the Stibnite Gold Project site were carried out under the supervision of Christopher Morgan, CPG, and Christopher Dail, CPG, both Qualified Persons as defined in NI 43-101 and in S-K 1300.

Samples were handled and shipped via Chain of Custody Procedures. Analyses were carried out by ALS Global Laboratories in their Reno and Elko, Nevada and Vancouver, British Columbia laboratories and by MSA Laboratories in Elko, Nevada and Langley, British Columbia.

All gold assays were determined using photon assay techniques, which include a 0.015 g/t lower reporting limit. data.title: Nvidia Has Real Problems-but Don't Fall For Fear Mongering — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Al Root

While accounting isn't always fun, it's necessary to understand — especially when numbers being thrown around aren't what they seem.

Nvidia stock is floundering in the wake of a scandal that has forced co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang to resign. Among the mountain of challenges the company is facing, investors have plenty to worry about — but the reemergence of accounting risks isn't one of them.

Did you know that Nvidia lists commitments and contingencies totaling $366 billion? And additional commitments of $56 billion? And another $108.5 billion in commitments to OpenAI? That adds up to $530.5 billion, a lot for a company that lists total liabilities on its balance sheet of $91 billion.

Well, yes. Because those figures are disclosed in quarterly filings. What's more, most of that money has little to do with circular financing, where Nvidia supplies money to customers who buy its hardware.

The bulk of that $530.5 billion — some $279 billion — are commitments representing future payment to suppliers such as memory chip makers. The money is disbursed over many years and flows through the income statement, accounting expert Robert Willens says.

Nvidia didn't respond to a request for comment about its accounting. Nvidia stock was down 2.2% in late trading on Friday at $162.56, leaving it down about 13% for the week. The S&P 500 was off 0.5%.

Broadcom reported $127 billion in similar purchase commitments. Its total balance sheet liabilities are $88 billion.

Both Nvidia and Broadcom's purchase committments are rising partly because of the high cost of memory chips.

Neither number is all that concerning, or out of line. Nvidia's chip business is roughly five times the size of Broadcom's.

Nvidia's commitments related to the AI buildout are closer to $200 billion, including more than $100 billion for OpenAI.

That is a lot of money, and circular financing is a risk to consider. But AI data-center hyperscalers are spending trillions, not billions. Most AI financing comes from cash flow, equity issuance, bonds, and loans.

Questions about Nvidia's willingness to extend financing terms to customers are certainly valid. It's just important to have the right numbers. Nvidia's customer finance commitments are closer to $200 billion, not half a trillion.

Write to Al Root at allen.root@dowjones.com
